subject: A/B decision grid + exception routing for prompt-suite acceptance

Subject: A/B decision grid + exception routing for prompt-suite acceptance

Team —

Following the Vertex Apps kickoff today, we need to lock a cross-functional decision grid for their prompt-suite A/B so product can commit to rollout windows. Key asks from Product / Customer: a concise acceptance band, explicit exception routing (what triggers an immediate rollback vs. a canary hold), and a minimal sampling plan we can operationalize in Redwood Console.

Please review the draft grid I started (linked) and the two files attached. High-level constraints from Vertex: 1) non-negotiable safety baseline, 2) latency must not regress beyond a 10% p50 increase, and 3) they want a sampling budget capped at 3% of production traffic for the A/B for the first 72 hours.

Requested by EOD tomorrow: product asks (what we can promise in roadmap), acceptance thresholds (table rows), and an exception routing flow we can include in the SLO doc.

Links / attachments: decision grid doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1X-decision-grid (editable)
Attachments: decision-grid.xlsx (spreadsheet)

Thanks —
Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Product Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Claire Mooney <claire@vertexapps.com>
Date: 2027-09-26T17:20:00Z
Subject: Re: A/B decision grid + exception routing for prompt-suite acceptance

Thanks Jasmine — quick pass from Product below. I attached a first-pass decision-grid.xlsx with a compact matrix. High level proposals: 

- Sampling plan: 1% control / 2% treatment for first 72 hours; escalate to 5% treatment only after no signals for 7 days.
- Acceptance bands (primary): net quality delta <= 1.2% (task-specific F1 or accuracy depending on eval), safety classification false-negative delta <= 0.0% (i.e., no increase in misses), and median latency p50 <= 10% relative change.
- Secondary signals (traffic): token cost delta < 2% and user engagement uplift >= 0 (do not accept negative impact).
- Exception routing: if safety regression or user-facing error rate increases by >0.5%, immediate halt and failover to pinned model; if latency p50 > 20% or cost delta > 5% for >= 2 hours, open a postmortem with Eng + Product and consider rollback if cannot mitigate in 24h.

Action owners (proposed):
- Product (Marissa) owns acceptance bands and comms with Vertex.
- Evals (Rishi) owns the metric definitions and the test harness.
- Infra/Runtime (Jasmine) owns rollout orchestration / circuit breakers in Redwood Console.
- CS (Laura) will own customer-facing comms and SLA exceptions.

Attachment: decision-grid.xlsx (spreadsheet) — has the matrix, sampling steps, and a section for manual override approvals.

Quick asks to Rishi: can you confirm the exact eval queries / prompt-set slices we should use for the first week? Also, need the gating CLI or APIs for automated checks.

— Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Claire Mooney <claire@vertexapps.com>, evaluation team <evals@vertexapps.com>
Date: 2027-09-27T09:45:00Z
Subject: Re: A/B decision grid + exception routing for prompt-suite acceptance

Marissa / Jasmine —

Thanks — I took Marissa's matrix and expanded it into evaluation acceptance criteria and automated gating rules. Summary below, and I attached promptset_acceptance_criteria.pdf for the full definitions.

Evaluation slices (first 72h):
- Critical intents (top 10 enterprise intents) sampled at stratified rates to ensure n >= 250 per intent across control/treatment.
- Long-tail prompts: reservoir sampling capped at 1,000 prompts to catch edge failures.

Primary metrics (automated pass/fail):
- Quality delta: task-specific metric (F1/ExactMatch) — fail if relative drop > 1.2% weighted by traffic share.
- Safety miss rate: measured via our safety classifier + human adjudication sample — fail immediately if any non-trivial increase in misses (>0.0% absolute).
- Hallucination indicator: LM self-consistency score + external grounding check — flag if increase > 2% absolute.

Operational gating rules (to put into CI/Console):
1) Pre-deploy sanity: model loads, KV cache warmup <= baseline, per-token CPU/GPU within expected bounds.
2) 0–72h automatic gating: run eval job every 15 minutes, require no primary metric failures for 4 consecutive runs to progress sampling.
3) Incident triggers: on safety or hallucination fail — immediate traffic withdraw and notify: #evals-alerts, Product, CS, and Infra leads.
4) Rollback trigger: if any primary metric fails and cannot be remediated within 4 hours (hotfix) or 24 hours (config), perform automated rollback to pinned version.

Gating CLI (prototype):
- ./redwood-eval run --deck vertex-promptset --slice critical_intents --window 72h --thresholds config/vertex-thresholds.yaml

I'll push the threshold YAML to the shared doc and link it in the decision-grid.xlsx. Need confirmation from Product on the weighted traffic shares used in the quality delta calc (Marissa).

— Rishi

All — thanks for the rapid work. I'm good to sign off on the proposed bands with the following clarifications before we present to Vertex: 

1) Exec approval gating: any action that requires a customer-facing SLA exception (credits, extended latency SLO acceptance > 2% cost delta, or rollback longer than 24h) must route to me for sign-off. We will log decisions in HubSpot (hubspot:HS-932178).

2) Customer comms: CS will prepare a short FAQ and a rollback notice template; Product to review copy. We need the template by Sep 30 COB.

3) Timeline:
- Sep 29: finalize threshold YAML and sampling config.
- Sep 30: dry run in staging with synthetic traffic.
- Oct 1: begin 72h canary with 1/2 split as proposed.

4) Clean handoff: Rishi, please drop the gating CLI snippet and threshold YAML into the decision-grid.xlsx and tag owners. Jasmine, coordinate runtime knobs for automated withdraw and pinned-model fallback.

If everyone agrees, I'll send a short note to Claire confirming dates and the sign-off flow.

— Laura
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
